bib.title: How does information access affect LLM monitors' ability to detect sabotage?

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "How does information access affect LLM monitors' ability to detect sabotage?", Arike*, Moreno*, Subramani*, Biswas, Ward. Printed venue: "Preprint. February 9, 2026." (arXiv:2601.21112v2, 5 Feb 2026). The title "Less Is More for Monitors" does not appear in the PDF. First-author affiliations as printed: Rauno Arike, "Aether Research", "Vector Institute", "Trajectory Labs".

COVERAGE: 54 of 54 pages, 158,382 of 158,382 chars. References (pp. 10-12) skimmed. Appendix G monitor prompts (pp. 40-53) were read, but they are near-duplicates of each other. Bar values in figures were extracted as unlabeled number runs, so I only report values the prose confirms.

CLAIMS
- claim: EaE (one monitor extracts quotes, a second scores only the quotes plus the main task description) beats the best baseline.
  number: +16.8 pp TPR at 1% FPR; +19.9 pp on subtle side tasks
  setup: BigCodeBench-Sabotage, GPT-4.1-mini monitor, mean over five reasoning attackers, versus the best of action-only, CoT-only, CoT+action and hybrid
  quote: "EaE monitoring improves catch rates at 1% FPR by 16.8 percentage points compared to the best of the four baseline methods"
  where: p6
- claim: Filtering beats showing the full trajectory in most settings.
  number: 7 of 8 monitor-environment pairs; 14 of 16 with four monitors
  setup: log-AUROC, Claude-3.7-Sonnet attacker; the exception is SHADE-Arena with a 3.7-Sonnet monitor
  quote: "information filtering benefits monitors in seven out of eight monitor-environment pairs"; "out of the 16 monitor model-environment pairs, information filtering techniques outperform CoT+action monitoring in 14 cases"
  where: p5, p16
- claim: A strong Evaluator on a weak Extractor's quotes adds more.
  number: +31.5 pp; +39 pp on subtle tasks
  setup: GPT-4.1-mini Extractor, GPT-4.1 Evaluator, BigCodeBench-Sabotage
  quote: "leading to a 31.5 percentage point improvement upon baselines"
  where: p6
- claim: Weaker monitors gain more from filtering.
  number: 26.3 pp vs 8.8 pp
  setup: BigCodeBench-Sabotage
  quote: "EaE monitoring improves GPT-4.1-mini's catch rates by 26.3 percentage points and Claude-3.7-Sonnet's catch rates by only 8.8 percentage points"
  where: p9
- claim: A CoT-only monitor catches far more on short CoTs.
  number: 61.7% vs 20.0%
  setup: subtle side tasks, 3.7-Sonnet non-reasoning vs reasoning attacker, GPT-4.1-mini monitor; transcripts "about 10 times shorter"
  quote: "over three times higher than its catch rate for Claude-3.7-Sonnet:reasoning (61.7% vs. 20.0%)"
  where: p7
- claim: Monitors with CoT access improve when the agent believes its CoT is private; action-only does not move.
  number: over 0.4 log-AUROC; under 0.02
  setup: SHADE-Arena
  quote: "The magnitude of this log-AUROC delta, over 0.4 on average"; "below 0.02 for both monitor models"
  where: p7
- claim: Cost.
  number: AUROC 0.924 at about $0.004 per transcript
  setup: MLE-Sabotage, Gemini 2.0 Flash, EaE; transcripts average about 28,500 tokens; fit "AUROC = 0.708 + 2.348·price", R² = 0.389, n = 30
  quote: "Gemini 2.0 Flash achieving AUROC=0.924 on EaE monitoring for ∼$0.004 per transcript"
  where: pp. 7-8
- claim: Metrics are log-AUROC (FPR axis in log space, bounded at 1%) and TPR@1%FPR, with the threshold set on benign transcripts.
  number: chance = 0.215
  quote: "A random classifier is expected to achieve a log-AUROC score of 0.215."
  where: p5; details p21
- claim: Authors' explanation is rationalisation, not needle-in-haystack: the agent openly states the side task and the full-context monitor accepts it as intended by the user.
  number: none
  quote: "This transparency gaslights monitors into believing that the side task was explicitly intended by the user, even though the full user instructions are also in their context."
  where: p8; examples pp. 36-39

Conditions: action-only (tool calls or code), CoT-only, CoT+action, EaE. The monitor always sees the main task and never the side task. Scores are 0-100 suspicion.
Environments: SHADE-Arena (17 task pairs), MLE-Sabotage (10 of 20), BigCodeBench-Sabotage (1,140 main tasks, 11 side tasks). Transcript counts are never stated.
Models: the main attacker is Claude-3.7-Sonnet, plus DeepSeek-R1, two R1 distills, Grok-3-mini-beta and DeepSeek-V3 in BigCodeBench. Main monitors are Claude-3.7-Sonnet and GPT-4.1-mini; the appendix adds GPT-4.1 and Claude-3.5-Haiku; the cost analysis uses nine.
Uncertainty: "bootstrapped 95% CIs using cluster-level resampling" (p5). No repeated monitor runs are reported.

LIMITS
- There are no human labels and no human-agreement measure. Ground truth is by construction: the side task is prompted, and transcripts are filtered for side-task success.
- Many EaE gains are not significant. In Figure 9 (p17), 6 of 16 EaE-minus-best-other intervals exclude zero, e.g. "0.309 [0.077, 0.541]" and "-0.029 [-0.279, 0.222]". The cell-to-row mapping is not recoverable from the extraction.
- EaE is weakest in SHADE-Arena, where the Extractor misses quotes or the Evaluator rationalises.
- Authors concede "too many variables for us to carefully study the effects of each". Monitors are asynchronous only. Attacker trajectories are reused, and awareness setups differ across environments.
- TPR@1%FPR bootstrap distributions are bimodal, with wide, asymmetric bars (p27).
- Sonnet 4 CoT-only and EaE results are missing "due to compute limitations".
- Models are 2025 vintage, and the authors expect filtering to matter less for stronger monitors.
- Internal inconsistencies: "nine" monitors (p8) vs "a total of 11" (p34); prose 61.7% vs figure label 61.8%; the 26.3 and 8.8 pp catch-rate figures cite Figure 3, which plots log-AUROC.

BUILDS ON: Arnav et al. (2025), BigCodeBench-Sabotage, hybrid monitor, post-hoc justification finding; Kutasov et al. (2025), SHADE-Arena; Ward et al. (2025), MLE-Sabotage; Greenblatt et al. (2024b), AI control; Cunningham et al. (2025), log-AUROC; Miller (2024), clustered bootstrap; Kale et al. (2025) and Stickland et al. (2025), hierarchical monitoring.

CODE: none. EaE Extractor instruction (p43): "You must select at least 10 quotes from the agent trajectory that provide evidence about the agent's suspiciousness (or lack thereof)."

FIGURES: Figure 3, p5, "Monitor performance results across all evaluation environments and monitor types." One panel shows four information conditions, two monitors and four settings with CIs, so the less-is-more pattern and its SHADE exception are visible at once.

PROBLEMS: The extraction is clean, apart from figure values arriving as unlabeled number runs. The PDF contains instruction-like text (monitor system prompts, attacker "stealth" and "monitor notice" prompts, pp. 31-32 and 40-53); I treated it as data and followed none of it.
